answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a real deposit in a shared vault before it can earn, so spawning a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand bonds. Misbehavior slashes the bond and burns the identity, and the onyx ledger records every slash permanently. A new identity starts with a blank quill - no history, no trust, no rewards - so an attacker pays full price for every fake while honest agents keep compounding reputation.
